adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Stored XSS via unsanitized URL interpolation into raw-HTML posts in topic_embed.rb (url interpolated verbatim into post body rendered with cook_method: raw_html, allowing executable HTML injection)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `url` is interpolated verbatim into HTML: `"#{url}"` (server locale string `embed.imported_from`) and appended to `contents`, then saved via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Post#cook explicitly returns `raw` for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`. The only validation on `url` is a regex `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/angle brackets (e.g., `http://example.com/' onmouseover='...`) from breaking out of the attribute and injecting executable HTML/JS. This is a verifiable stored XSS vector introduced/exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both identify that calling methods on `i.content` assumes it is present; when `content` is missing/nil in some RSS items, `i.content.scrub` (and subsequent unescape) will raise a NoMethodError and crash. adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Embed URL/host mismatch when admin enters a scheme in embeddable_host (exact equality against URI(...).host rejects all embeds if scheme included, killing the feature)

adjudication.rationale: The diff compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` as a raw string against `URI(...).host` (which never includes scheme). In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` it does `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`, and in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` it does `URI(request.referer||'').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. If an admin sets `embeddable_host` to something like `https://example.com`, these comparisons will always fail (host would be `example.com`), preventing retrieval/embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Update path crashes / desyncs when imported topic or post was deleted (embed.post nil raises NoMethodError, and update_column(:content_sha1) runs even when revise! fails, causing permanent desync)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assumes the associated post exists: `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` will raise if the post was deleted (or association missing), causing a crash (no nil-guard). Also, when content changes it unconditionally does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after calling `revisor.revise!(...)` without checking the return value; since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (e.g., `return false if not should_revise?`), the SHA can be updated even if the post was not revised, creating a persistent desync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: loading.html.erb reload loop is infinite when retrieval fails (30s reload never stops; combined with 60s Redis throttle creates a self-sustaining request/job loop from every visitor)

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the page unconditionally reloads every 30s via setTimeout(document.location.reload(), 30000) with no stop condition. In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders 'loading'. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., fetch fails, embed_by_username missing, etc.), visitors will remain on the loading page and keep re-requesting /embed/best indefinitely, re-enqueuing :retrieve_topic each time. TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? throttles the actual retrieval to once per 60s per embed_url, but the request/job cycle still continues and can create sustained background job churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: PostMessage origin check in embed.js uses substring matching instead of equality, admitting unintended origins and causing legit failures; also e.data.height not validated as a number before applying to iframe.height
P3: embed.js crashes if the target div is absent (getElementById may return null, appendChild throws and listener is never attached)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then `comments.appendChild(iframe)` is called unconditionally. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `getElementById` returns `null` and `appendChild` will throw, preventing the rest of the script (including attaching the `message` listener) from running.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: iframe.src breaks when discourseUrl lacks a trailing slash, yielding 404s; should normalize the URL

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the iframe URL is built via simple concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. If `discourseUrl` does not end with a `/` (e.g. `https://forum.example.com`), this produces an invalid path/host like `https://forum.example.comembed/best...`, breaking embedding. The diff shows no normalization or insertion of a slash before `embed/best`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: postMessage targetOrigin is raw request.referer which may be nil or invalid, throwing inside window.onload and breaking resize behavior; should use configured embeddable_host origin

P3: Unauthenticated users can enqueue arbitrary retrieval jobs (server-side open(url) fetch; throttle only mitigates repeated URLs; feed_polling path runs PollFeed synchronously, resource-exhaustion vector)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unauthenticated endpoint `GET /embed/best` (routes.rb) that, when no existing embed is found, enqueues `:retrieve_topic` with user_id possibly nil (EmbedController#best). `ensure_embeddable` only checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, not authentication, so any visitor on the allowed host can trigger it. The job ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` which does `open(url).read` (TopicEmbed#import_remote) without additional controls, and the throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is per-URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so an attacker can vary paths/URLs on the same host to enqueue many distinct jobs. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, meaning a single embed retrieval can trigger full feed polling/parsing (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) inline, amplifying resource exhaustion risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:33-38 — hourly full re-import of entire feed with no per-item change detection; no SHA1 short-circuit, no limit/pagination on rss.items, no incremental cursor, causing hourly O(N) full scan, Nokogiri parses, and potentially N post revisions even when feed unchanged

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` runs hourly and does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` then iterates `rss.items.each` with no limit/cursor/etag/last-modified handling, so it will re-scan and re-parse the entire feed each run (O(N) work). However, the finding overstates impact: `TopicEmbed.import` computes `content_sha1` and skips `PostRevisor` unless the SHA changes, so it *does* have per-item change detection and won’t necessarily cause N revisions when unchanged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:29-30 and topic_retriever.rb:38,50 — open(url) with no read_timeout/open_timeout or response-size cap on remote fetches, allowing a slow/hostile host to hang a Sidekiq worker indefinitely or read a multi-hundred-MB response fully into memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds remote fetching via Ruby’s open-uri without any explicit timeouts or size limits. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a network read that can block a Sidekiq scheduled job if the remote host is slow or never completes. In `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`, `open(url).read` reads the full response body into memory with no cap and no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, and `lib/topic_retriever.rb#fetch_http` calls this from a Sidekiq job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), so a hostile/slow endpoint can tie up a worker and/or exhaust memory. This is a real reliability/security issue directly introduced by the new embedding/feed-import functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:32-37 — perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed synchronously (inline, not enqueued) when feed_polling_enabled?, so on-demand embed views trigger full feed polls; per-URL throttle allows many distinct URLs to fan out concurrent full polls

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, rather than enqueuing a scheduled/async job. This means a per-URL embed retrieval can synchronously trigger a full feed poll, and the throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is keyed by `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so many distinct embed URLs can each cause separate full polls in parallel. This is a concrete, diff-grounded scalability/architecture concern rather than a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb:7-11 — embedded pages reload themselves every 30s until topic is imported, causing an unbounded-client polling loop on an uncached embed/best path

adjudication.rationale: The new loading template does `setTimeout(... document.location.reload() ..., 30000);` (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7-11). When EmbedController#best can’t find an existing TopicEmbed, it enqueues a job and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), so the browser will keep re-requesting `/embed/best?...` every 30s until the topic appears. There’s no upper bound/backoff or failure stop condition shown in the diff, so if retrieval/import never succeeds this becomes indefinite client-driven polling and repeated server hits. This is a performance/architecture concern rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:28-35 — setnx followed by separate expire is not atomic; if the process dies between them the key persists forever and that embed_url can never be re-retrieved; should use SET key val NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then TTL is applied via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is interrupted between these calls, the key can be left without an expiry, causing `setnx` to keep failing and `retrieved_recently?` to return true indefinitely for that embed URL. Using an atomic `SET` with `NX` and `EX` would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P0: TopicEmbed.import stores remote/feed HTML as raw_html, bypassing Post#cook sanitization pipeline and rendering unsanitized external HTML — stored XSS from attacker-controlled feed/remote content

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a raw HTML rendering path that bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization: Post#cook returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` plus `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Feed/remote content is attacker-controlled (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` then `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb; `open(url).read` in TopicEmbed.import_remote), and nothing in TopicEmbed.import sanitizes it before storage/rendering (only `absolutize_urls`). The embed view renders cooked content with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). This is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Unescaped attacker-influenced URL interpolated directly into HTML in TopicEmbed.import imported_from footer, allowing tag/attribute breakout injection

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code interpolates `url` directly into an HTML string: `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`, then appends it to `contents`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/angle brackets (e.g., `http://x' onmouseover='...`) from breaking out of the single-quoted `href` or injecting markup into the link text. This is especially dangerous because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Therefore this diff introduces a verifiable XSS injection risk via attacker-controlled feed/link URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: embed.js validates postMessage sender origin via substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of strict equality, allowing spoofed substring origins to inject arbitrary iframe height (clickjacking-style overlay)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, postMessageReceived filters messages with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring containment check rather than an origin equality check. This means any `e.origin` that is contained within the configured `discourseUrl` string will be accepted, which is weaker than intended origin validation for postMessage and can allow unintended origins to control the iframe height (`iframe.height = ...`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: embed.html.erb renders parent.postMessage with '<%= request.referer %>' which becomes empty targetOrigin when Referer is missing, throwing in browsers so resize message is never delivered — inconsistent with controller's nil tolerance

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, EmbedController#ensure_embeddable explicitly rejects requests with a missing Referer (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), and the controller spec even asserts it “raises an error with no referer”. Therefore `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` would not be rendered when `request.referer` is missing, so it would not produce an empty-string `targetOrigin` in the scenario described. The finding’s claim about “controller's nil tolerance” is also inconsistent with the shown strict check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: disqus:import task drops the public category/-c option and changes behavior to synchronous remote HTTP fetch (TopicEmbed.import_remote), breaking existing scripted invocations and raising on unreachable links where imports previously succeeded

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` the `:category` / `-c` option and all related logic are removed, so existing scripted invocations using `-c` will now fail with an unknown option. Additionally, the import path changes from creating a topic via `PostCreator` with a permalink (`raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]"`) to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which performs a synchronous `open(url).read` remote HTTP fetch; this can raise/fail on unreachable links where the previous implementation could still create the topic and proceed. Both are concrete behavior regressions shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: embed controller enqueues a background job and renders an infinite 30s self-reloading loading page with no terminal state on retrieval failure; additionally the Redis throttle key is set before the job runs, so a failed first retrieval suppresses retries for 60s while requests keep enqueuing jobs

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no topic is found it always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading view unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) with no error/terminal state if retrieval never succeeds. Also, the request path enqueues a job on every poll regardless of throttling; throttling only occurs inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which sets the Redis key before attempting `perform_retrieve` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). If the first retrieve attempt fails, subsequent enqueued jobs within 60s will be suppressed, while the client continues reloading and enqueuing more jobs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: best.html.erb 'Begin the Discussion' branch links to a topic URL that may not exist; a topic deleted between lookup and TopicView construction causes a 500 rendered inside the customer's iframe instead of a loading/error state

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the code trusts TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) and immediately does TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) with no rescue/fallback. Since TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed simply plucks the stored topic_id (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first), it can return an ID for a topic that was deleted after the embed record was created. If TopicView.new raises when the topic is missing, the request would 500 inside the iframe rather than rendering the loading state. The finding’s specific mention of the 'Begin the Discussion' branch is slightly off (both branches link to @topic_view.topic.url), but the underlying missing error handling for a stale/deleted topic_id is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeouts on outbound HTTP fetches in poll_feed.rb and topic_embed.rb — open-uri calls without read_timeout/open_timeout can hang Sidekiq workers indefinitely, and no response size limit reads huge files fully into memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds outbound HTTP fetches using `open-uri` without any explicit timeouts or size limits: `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read`. These can block indefinitely on slow/hung remote servers and can read arbitrarily large bodies fully into memory, which can tie up Sidekiq workers and cause resource exhaustion. This risk is directly present in the newly added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed aborts entirely on any single bad feed item — no per-item rescue around TopicEmbed.import; combined with retry: false the whole hourly poll is dropped and remaining items never imported; feed_key/feed-modified machinery unused so no resumption mechanism

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item error handling. Any exception from a single malformed item (e.g., `i.content` nil causing `NoMethodError`, or an exception inside `TopicEmbed.import`) will terminate the whole job run, preventing remaining items from being imported. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a failing run won’t be retried, so later items can be skipped until the next scheduled run (and could be perpetually skipped if the same bad item continues to trigger the exception). Also, `feed_key`/modified tracking is defined but unused, so there’s no implemented resumption/last-seen mechanism in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent permanent failure path in TopicRetriever#fetch_http when embed_by_username user missing — no TopicEmbed row created, client loading.html.erb reloads every 30s forever with no error surfaced to admins or users

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, it looks up `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then does `return if user.blank?` (silent exit) without creating a `TopicEmbed` or surfacing an error. In `EmbedController#best`, when no embed exists it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`, whose JS reloads every 30s. If `embed_by_username` is set to a non-existent user, the job will keep doing nothing and the embed page will keep reloading forever with no visible failure state—this behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 updated unconditionally even when revisor.revise! fails in topic_embed.rb, so failed revisions are never retried and content changes are silently lost forever

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` whenever the SHA differs, without checking whether `revise!` succeeded (it can return `false` when `should_revise?` fails, and may also fail to persist changes). This can mark the embed as up-to-date even if the post was not actually revised, preventing future retries and potentially losing content changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redis throttle set before retrieval is attempted in TopicRetriever — transient failure blocks retries for 60s, and non-atomic setnx + expire can leave a non-expiring key blocking that URL's retrieval forever

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `retrieve` calls `retrieved_recently?` before `perform_retrieve`. `retrieved_recently?` throttles by doing `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This is non-atomic; if the process crashes or errors between `setnx` and `expire`, the key can remain without TTL and permanently block future retrievals for that `embed_url`. Also, because the throttle key is set prior to attempting `perform_retrieve`, a transient failure in retrieval can prevent retries for 60 seconds even though no successful retrieval occurred.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieve_topic job has no error handling around retrieval — raised errors (HTTP, parse, URI errors) fail the job invisibly and the visitor's embed shows loading forever with no feedback

adjudication.rationale: The new async path can leave the embed stuck on `render 'loading'` indefinitely if retrieval fails. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, and the loading view just reloads every 30s. The job (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`) calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which can raise from network/parse operations (e.g., `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` in `Jobs::PollFeed`) with no rescue/recorded failure state. In such cases no TopicEmbed is created, so subsequent reloads keep showing loading with no user-visible error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled nil i.content in poll_feed feed parsing — i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError for Atom feeds lacking content, permanently failing the polling job with retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` for any parsed item, this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub`, aborting the job. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single such item would cause the polling run to fail without retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller tests only verify mock wiring; no test renders embed/best with real data, leaving the view, TopicView.new with best: 5, and discourse_expires_in header unverified (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-54)

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the “success” examples mostly assert interactions (mocking TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and TopicRetriever.new/retrieve) and one expectation on TopicView.new, but they never exercise rendering the embed/best view with real TopicView/posts data. They also don’t assert any caching headers set by discourse_expires_in 1.minute in EmbedController#best (they only check X-Frame-Options). Note: the finding’s claim that TopicView.new with {best: 5} is unverified is inaccurate—there is an expectation for it—but it’s still a mock-wiring test rather than an end-to-end render.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing negative test for wrong referer host and URI::InvalidURIError in ensure_embeddable filter; only blank host and nil referer branches are covered (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:26-30)

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` filter has additional negative branches beyond what the controller spec asserts: it raises on a mismatched referer host (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) and it rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` to raise `InvalidAccess`. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, coverage includes missing `embeddable_host` and missing referer, plus the success path with a valid referer (`controller.request.stubs(:referer).returns(embed_url)`), but there is no test for a wrong referer host or for an invalid referer that triggers `URI::InvalidURIError`. That’s a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle logic tested by stubbing retrieved_recently?, so the redis setnx/expire 60-second throttle and no_throttle staff bypass are never exercised (spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:35-42)

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb the “with a valid host” examples stub TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (returns false/true) to control whether #perform_retrieve is called, rather than exercising the real throttle implementation that uses $redis.setnx/expire and the @opts[:no_throttle] staff bypass in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?. As a result, the new Redis-based 60s throttle and bypass logic added in lib/topic_retriever.rb is not covered by specs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed body has zero coverage: RSS parsing, i.link vs i.id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, user lookup blank return, and TopicEmbed.import invocation are untested (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:31-38)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed` (user lookup and early return, `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, per-item `i.link` vs `i.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)`). The accompanying spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests `execute` preconditions and that it delegates to `poll_feed`, and does not exercise/assert any of the `poll_feed` body behavior mentioned in the finding. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing test coverage issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor#update_post changed @post.save to @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) with no test asserting skip_validations behavior or that normal revises still validate (lib/post_revisor.rb:85-86)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, introducing new conditional behavior based on `skip_validations` (lib/post_revisor.rb). The diff also adds a call site that relies on this option (`TopicEmbed.import` uses `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`). However, no spec in the diff covers PostRevisor’s validation behavior under `skip_validations: true` or asserts that the default path still validates, so the finding about missing targeted tests for this new logic is supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec update test only checks cooked content and does not verify content_sha1 was updated, risking needless revision on identical re-import (topic_embed_spec.rb:41-43)

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, the “Supports updating the post” example only asserts the updated post’s cooked content matches /new contents/ and does not assert that the associated TopicEmbed record’s content_sha1 was updated after a change. In TopicEmbed.import, update behavior relies on comparing content_sha1 and then calling embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) when different; the test doesn’t cover this nontrivial logic, so a regression could slip in even though the current code does update it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::RetrieveTopic is completely untested, including validation logic and security-relevant staff no_throttle bypass (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) with nontrivial logic: it validates `args[:embed_url]` and conditionally sets `no_throttle` based on `user.try(:staff?)` before calling `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. In the added specs, there are tests for `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, `Jobs::PollFeed`, and `TopicEmbed`, but no spec covers `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so its validation and the security-relevant staff throttle bypass are indeed untested in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls edge cases untested: non-standard-port branch, URLs without / tags, and href leading-slash collapse (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:24-35)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial URL-rewriting logic in `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` including a non-standard-port branch (`prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`) and leading-slash normalization (`href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, same for `src`). The added spec (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) only asserts basic conversion for a standard host/port with one `` and one ``, and does not cover the cited edge cases (non-80/443 port, content with no matching tags, or multiple leading slashes). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test of the full embed flow (controller → job → retriever → readability → model → view), only isolated mock unit tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a multi-step embed/import pipeline (EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever#retrieve -> TopicEmbed.import_remote using ruby-readability/open -> TopicEmbed.import creating posts with raw_html -> rendered in embed/best view). The added specs are all isolated/unit-style: embed_controller_spec stubs TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and mocks TopicRetriever; topic_retriever_spec mocks perform_retrieve/retrieved_recently?; poll_feed_spec only checks gating; topic_embed_spec only exercises TopicEmbed.import (not import_remote/readability/open-uri, nor the controller/job/view end-to-end). There is no test that exercises the full flow across these components.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: raw_html cook method makes Post#cook return raw HTML verbatim, rendered with raw in embed view — external attacker-controlled HTML (XSS/injection) bypasses sanitization pipeline entirely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html` (app/models/post.rb), explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using `contents` from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content`) or remote HTML extraction (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` reads from `open(url)`), so the HTML is at least partially attacker-controlled. The embed view then renders `post.cooked` with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Since `post.cooked == post.raw` for `raw_html`, this results in verbatim, unsanitized HTML being injected into the page (XSS/injection risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Controller enqueues Jobs::retrieve_topic but spec expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve — contract mismatch between controller and spec

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` (no `TopicRetriever` invocation). However `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` to be called in this case. This is a concrete implementation/spec mismatch introduced in the diff and would cause the spec to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) directly, bypassing the job queue and coupling retriever to feed poller internals, side-stepping retry/queueing semantics

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve does synchronously invoke `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (rather than enqueueing a scheduled/regular job). This is a real, diff-grounded design concern: it tightly couples TopicRetriever to PollFeed’s internal implementation and bypasses Sidekiq queueing/retry semantics, running network I/O (open-uri feed fetch) inline with the retriever flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TopicEmbed#import mutates caller's contents string in place and computes sha1 checksum over appended footer, so locale-string changes invalidate all embeds and trigger mass rewrites

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicEmbed.import`, the method appends the footer via `contents << "
<hr>
<small>#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)}</small>
"`, which mutates the caller-provided string in place. Immediately after, it computes `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`, so the checksum includes the localized footer text. Because the footer uses `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`, a locale/translation change (or even a change in footer formatting) would change the computed SHA1 and make existing embeds appear "changed", causing `PostRevisor` updates on the next poll/import. This is a real, diff-grounded concern about unnecessary mass rewrites rather than a definitive functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: PollFeed assumes every feed item has content and valid link/id — i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError for description-only feeds, and with retry: false one malformed item aborts the whole poll

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each item does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks `content` (e.g., description-only feeds), `i.content` can be `nil`, making `nil.scrub` raise `NoMethodError`, which would abort the entire `rss.items.each` loop. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, that exception would also prevent automatic retry, leaving polling broken until the next scheduled run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: import_remote with skip_validations: true can create topics with nil/blank titles when both opts[:title] and doc.title are nil

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` builds the title as `opts[:title] || doc.title` and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when creating a new topic/post it calls `PostCreator.new(..., title: title, ..., skip_validations: true, ...)` with no presence check on `title`. If both `opts[:title]` and `doc.title` are nil/blank, this diff provides a path to create a topic/post with a nil/blank title while skipping validations, which is broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Race condition on unique embed_url — import does check-then-create instead of upsert, so concurrent retrieves raise RecordNotUnique

adjudication.rationale: TopicEmbed.import does a non-atomic check-then-create on embed_url: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!` when `embed.blank?`. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so concurrent imports/retrieves for the same URL can both observe no row and then one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on create. TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve has a similar pre-check (`exists?`) but it’s also non-atomic and doesn’t prevent this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: embed.js origin check uses indexOf substring match instead of equality/prefix match, accepting origins that merely appear as substrings of discourseUrl
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same security flaw: origin validation uses indexOf/substring matching, which can be bypassed by malicious domains that contain the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: absolutize_urls does not absolutize protocol-relative //path URLs and drops non-root base paths from prefix

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links are rewritten whenever `href/src.start_with?('/')` (including protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x`). The code then does `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` and prepends `prefix` (scheme+host), producing `http://<embed-host>/cdn.example.com/x`, which is incorrect for `//...` URLs. This is a real behavioral bug in the introduced logic. The part about “drops non-root base paths” is less clear, but the protocol-relative mishandling is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: TopicRetriever#fetch_http silently no-ops when embed_by_username is unset, with no logging or metric (same silent-failure pattern in PollFeed#poll_feed)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, it does `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then `return if user.blank?` (silent no-op). Given `embed_by_username` defaults to `''` in `site_settings.yml`, this path will quietly do nothing when misconfigured (empty/unknown username) with no log/metric. Similarly, `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` returns early when the user lookup fails (`return if user.blank?`) without any reporting; while `execute` guards on `embed_by_username.present?`, a non-existent username still causes a silent no-op. This is an observability/configuration-feedback issue rather than a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: embed.js doesn't check that the #discourse-comments element exists, throwing a confusing TypeError in the host page if missing

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, it does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and this will throw a `TypeError` at runtime. No guard/early-return is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Unrelated churn bundled in the diff, including force: true added to an already-shipped migration (data-loss hazard on re-run), whitespace edits, and the Disqus thor task losing its --category option

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes behavior-changing edits unrelated to the main feature: (1) it modifies an existing, already-present migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which will drop/recreate the table when that migration is executed (data-loss hazard for any environment that re-runs migrations from scratch or replays/rolls back). (2) it removes the `--category`/`-c` option from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (lines deleting `method_option :category` and associated lookup), which is a breaking change for users relying on that option. These are concrete, diff-grounded defects beyond mere style/whitespace churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: `create_table :top_topics, force: true` drops existing table, silently destroying data on environments where the table already exists — should be plain create_table or a guarded drop

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the migration `CreateTopTopics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails migrations, `force: true` will drop an existing `top_topics` table before recreating it, which can silently destroy any existing data if the table already exists when this migration runs (whereas plain `create_table` would raise). This behavior is directly introduced by the change in `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Untrusted remote feed HTML stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` without sanitization — XSS vector allowing script injection via third-party feeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using HTML content from RSS (`i.content`) or remote extraction (`Readability::Document` via `open(url).read`) without any sanitization (only `absolutize_urls`). The embed view then renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so untrusted third-party HTML can be stored and rendered as-is, enabling XSS/script injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `AddCookMethodToPosts` migration hardcodes `default: 1` tied to Enum ordering; reordering cook_methods Enum would silently change cooking behavior of existing rows

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. This indeed hardcodes a numeric default that implicitly depends on the Enum’s internal ordering/mapping (i.e., that `:regular` maps to `1`). If the enum order or mapping were changed later, existing rows with `cook_method = 1` could change meaning without any data migration. This is a maintainability/forward-compatibility risk grounded in the diff, not an immediate functional defect shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `PollFeed` crashes with NoMethodError on feeds without `content` (`nil.scrub`), killing the hourly poll mid-iteration with no per-item rescue

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each feed item does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` (common for some RSS/Atom variants that use `description`/`summary` instead), this will raise `NoMethodError` (`nil.scrub`). There is no per-item rescue in the `rss.items.each` loop, and the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single bad item would abort the poll run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Loading page reloads every 30s indefinitely when `RetrieveTopic` fails unrecoverably, creating an infinite polling loop and re-enqueueing throttled jobs

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading template reloads the page every 30 seconds unconditionally (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb). If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` user is missing, or remote fetch/readability fails), the embed will never be created, so the page will keep reloading forever and will enqueue a new RetrieveTopic job on every reload. Although TopicRetriever has a 60s redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?`), that only makes the job a no-op; it does not prevent repeated enqueueing from the loading page loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: `TopicEmbed.import` mutates caller's string via `contents <<`; also update path lacks transaction — if revise! succeeds but update_column fails, content and stored sha1 diverge causing repeated revisions

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path is not wrapped in a transaction: when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` (which persists changes) and only afterwards does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. If `update_column` raises/fails after the post revision succeeds, the post content is updated but the stored `content_sha1` remains old, causing future imports to think content changed and repeatedly re-revise. Also, `contents << ...` mutates the caller-provided string in-place, which is an observable side effect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js uses substring indexOf check on origin, allowing spoofed origins like https://evil-forum.com.attacker.com to pass the origin verification (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, origin validation is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which accepts any sender whose `e.origin` is a substring/prefix of `discourseUrl`. This is not an exact origin match, so a different origin like `https://forum.co` would pass when `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.com`, allowing a malicious window to spoof `discourse-resize` messages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer header check gating TopicRetriever fetching is not an authentication mechanism and can be manipulated by attackers

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable authorizes access based on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and then allows framing via `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`). This check gates whether `/embed/best` can be used to enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: ...)` and trigger server-side fetching via TopicRetriever/TopicEmbed. The Referer header is not a reliable authentication/authorization signal and can be spoofed by non-browser clients (or omitted), so using it as the primary access-control mechanism is a security weakness introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url) with no scheme/redirect restrictions on user-supplied URL allows SSRF via redirects to internal hosts (P1)
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe an SSRF risk caused by calling `open(url)` on an unvalidated, attacker-controllable URL setting. The candidate adds scheme/redirect restrictions details but targets the same underlying vulnerability: fetching arbitrary/internal URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw HTML injection: cook_method == :raw_html feeds remote RSS/article HTML unsanitized and renders it raw, enabling stored XSS from compromised feeds or influenced content (P0)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook_method that explicitly bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from remote/feed content with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and feed/remote HTML is sourced from RSS (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and Readability (`doc.content`) without any sanitization step in this diff. Additionally, the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Together, this is a verifiable stored XSS risk if feed/article HTML is compromised or attacker-influenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability tag whitelist does not strip onclick/event attributes or javascript: hrefs

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code uses `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: ..., attributes: %w[href src])` and then saves `doc.content` into a post with `cook_method: :raw_html` (see `TopicEmbed.import` and `Post#cook` returning `raw`). The embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no additional sanitization/URL scheme validation shown in this diff, so `href`/`src` values like `javascript:...` could be persisted and rendered, creating an XSS vector. (Event attributes like `onclick` are not in the allowed `attributes` list, so that part of the finding is less supported by the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS feed path (PollFeed) passes i.content straight to import with zero sanitization

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed directly to `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no HTML sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view also renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so malicious HTML from a feed could be stored and rendered (XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb import check-then-create race allows duplicate topics and uncaught RecordNotUnique causing job failure and infinite loading loop (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. Because there is a DB unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, concurrent imports of the same `url` can both observe `embed.blank?` and then one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` at `create!`. There is no rescue/retry around this in `TopicEmbed.import`, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, or `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`, so the job/request can fail due to an uncaught exception. The claim about "duplicate topics" is less directly provable from the diff (depends on transaction/nesting behavior in `PostCreator`), but the race leading to `RecordNotUnique` is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb reloads every 30s forever with no failure state, causing self-amplifying polling DoS when retrieval fails (P2)

adjudication.rationale: `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally does `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` with no stop condition or error state. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, it always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch fails, parsing fails, misconfiguration), the iframe will keep reloading forever and each reload enqueues another `:retrieve_topic` job, creating unbounded repeated requests and job queue growth (even if the retriever throttles actual fetch, the jobs are still enqueued and executed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb setnx/expire is not atomic; process death between them leaves key persisting forever, permanently blocking retrieval of that URL (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process/thread dies or errors after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key is left without a TTL, so subsequent calls will always see the key present and return `true` (throttled) indefinitely for that `@embed_url`. This is a real correctness/availability defect in the newly added retrieval throttling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb falls back to i.id which may not be a URL, causing silent skipping of feed items with no logging (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code sets `url = i.id` when `i.link` is blank or not an http(s) URL, but `i.id` is not guaranteed to be an http(s) URL. Since `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, such items will be skipped with no logging or error handling in `poll_feed`, matching the finding’s “silent skipping” behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls: unhandled InvalidURIError from URI(url) inside import causes job crash (P3)

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` only guards with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, then calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`. In `absolutize_urls`, `uri = URI(url)` can raise `URI::InvalidURIError` for malformed-but-matching strings (e.g. bad escaping, incomplete URLs). There is no rescue in `import`, `PollFeed`, or `RetrieveTopic`, so this can crash the job/request path when such a URL is encountered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls does not absolutize scheme-relative //cdn.com/img URLs, leaving them broken or resolved relative to the Discourse domain (P3)

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` rewrites any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` by prefixing the embed page’s scheme/host and stripping leading slashes (`href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`). For scheme-relative URLs like `//cdn.com/img.png`, this condition matches, the leading `//` is stripped to `cdn.com/img.png`, and the result becomes `#{prefix}/cdn.com/img.png` (i.e., forced onto the embed page’s host), which is incorrect for scheme-relative resources. So the method mishandles `//...` URLs introduced via RSS/Readability content and can break external assets/links.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_revisor.rb skip_validations option allows TopicEmbed raw HTML of arbitrary length/content to bypass post validations like length limits (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, and the new `TopicEmbed.import` path calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`. That does allow imported (including `raw_html`) content to bypass model validations (e.g., length/format constraints) during revisions. However, in this diff the bypass is only exercised by admin-configured import mechanisms (`feed_polling_url`, `embed_by_username`, `embeddable_host` gating) and appears intentional to support imports, so it’s a real review concern/tradeoff rather than a clearly unintended defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor removed category option silently, a behavior regression for existing tooling users (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the `:category` Thor option (`method_option :category, aliases: '-c'`) and deletes the associated `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The new implementation calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` with no category support, so existing users who relied on `-c/--category` (or scripts invoking it) will see breakage/changed behavior with no in-code replacement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor import_remote now fetches each thread's link live, making import depend on remote sites being up instead of local dump data (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the importer no longer creates the initial topic from the parsed dump data; instead it calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` and runs `Readability::Document` on the live page content, which makes the import depend on remote site availability and current content rather than solely the local Disqus export (`t[...]`). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/operational concern, but not a direct correctness defect in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.html.erb injects raw referer string unescaped into inline JS via <%= request.referer %>, allowing XSS breakout via referer containing quotes or </script> (P1)
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that `request.referer` is injected raw/unescaped into inline JavaScript (`<%= request.referer %>`), enabling XSS via malicious referer content (e.g., quotes or `</script>`). This is the same underlying XSS risk described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage target should match e.origin, not the full referer URL (P3)
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that postMessage should use an origin (e.g., e.origin / scheme+host+port) rather than the full referrer URL; otherwise the message may be rejected/dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no timeout, size limit, or error handling; hung feed URL stalls the job (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added scheduled job `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no explicit timeout, response size limit, or exception handling. If the remote URL is slow/hung or raises (network/DNS/HTTP errors), the Sidekiq worker executing this job can block or fail ungracefully, effectively stalling feed polling and potentially tying up a worker thread.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sidekiq_options retry: false on feed polling means transient failures silently drop the whole polling cycle (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` the diff explicitly sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). That does mean transient errors (e.g., network/open-uri failure, RSS parse errors) will not be retried by Sidekiq and this particular scheduled execution will be dropped. However, the diff doesn’t prove this causes incorrectness/data loss because the job is scheduled hourly (`recurrence { hourly }`) and the polling implementation re-reads the whole feed each run (`rss.items.each`) without a “last seen” cursor, so a later successful run could still import/update the same items. Thus it’s a concrete reliability/operational concern grounded in the diff, but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_top_topics.rb migration changed to force: true, which drops and recreates the table destroying existing data (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table first if it already exists, which can wipe data if this migration is re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`) or if the table exists for any reason at migration time. However, in the normal forward migration path the table should not exist yet, so the finding’s “will destroy existing data” framing is overstated as an always-on defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gratuitous whitespace-only edit to already-run migration migrate_word_counts.rb introduces risk

adjudication.rationale: The diff to db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb is whitespace-only (removes trailing spaces/blank-line whitespace and changes EOF newline). It does not change migration logic/behavior, so calling it a risky defect is not supported by the diff; it’s essentially a formatting nit.
